$comment: The source of sf-resizer's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/resizer (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

min.x-summary: The narrowest width: a CSS length, tokens included
min.summary: The narrowest width, a CSS length (tokens and percentages of the panel's parent too).

max.x-summary: The widest width: a CSS length, tokens included
max.summary: The widest width, a CSS length.

property.summary: A CSS custom property the width is written to on the target; empty writes inline-size.

target.summary: A selector of the closest ancestor that is the panel; empty is the parent.

step.x-summary: Pixels an arrow key moves; Shift, PageUp and PageDown move four steps
step.summary: Pixels an arrow key moves; Shift moves four steps.

storage-key.summary: Remembers the width (and a fold) in this browser as the view preference sf-resizer/<key> (SF.Preferences); a double click forgets it.

label.summary: The accessible name; defaults to the page language's «Resize».

collapsible.summary: The panel folds to its edge when dragged past min by half of min, and Enter folds it and gives back the width it had; a «Show» button on the edge brings it back. Off by default.

value.x-summary: A width the host keeps for the person, in pixels (0: folded); it wins over this browser's memory
value.summary: A width in pixels the host keeps (a person's settings); it wins over the browser's memory. With collapsible, 0 is a folded panel.

default.$comment: The handle draws nothing of its own: the host is the separator, its line a ::after of its own sheet. There is no markup to write (§5.1).

accessibility.$comment: The host is a focusable separator (aria-orientation vertical by its role) that controls its panel (aria-controls); aria-valuenow is the share of the way from min to max, 0-100 (0: the narrowest, or folded), with the words in aria-valuetext («27 %», «Свёрнуто»); its description (title) says how to use it. ArrowLeft and ArrowRight follow the writing direction and the edge. Enter folds and restores a collapsible panel and restores the default width of one that is not; Space does nothing. A disabled handle and one below the layout's split step are out of the Tab order.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-resizer for the shim (core/js/aliases.js, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), detail-adds (the new detail holds the old fields), attribute-and-property, host-attribute (no shim), manifest-only (the DOM name does not change), retired (no new name; kept and noted by the component until the date).

rows.note: the old name follows with the same detail {width, phase}
rows.summary: The width changed: while dragging (move), after a drag or a key (end), or back to the stylesheet's width (reset).

x-summary: A handle on a panel's edge that changes the panel's width by a drag, the keyboard or a double click back to the default, within limits; optionally remembered in the browser.
x-renamed: events.sf-resize → resize (sf-resizer-resize): the DOM name takes the tag (§8, vocabulary §7)
settings.step: a numeral → number (§16 item 29); value: a width in pixels → number, nullable
x-decisions: version 1.3.0 (owner decision C158, resizer study control/research/2026-11-14-resizer.md, prototype prototypes/resizer-study.html): a minor. (1) The strip of 1.2.0 (24, 44 under a finger, centred on the edge; the panel's own border is the line at rest, the 2 px line after --sf-duration-normal, a focus ring around the strip) is the accepted look. (2) collapsible (boolean, off by default): a drag past min by half of min folds the panel to its edge -- data-folded on the panel (the prototype's name), its width written 0, its content hidden -- and back over that line opens it again; Enter folds and gives back the width it had (APG window splitter), a double click is the default width (and open), Space does nothing (it reverted before); an arrow that widens opens a folded panel at min; a «Показать» (Show) sf-button-icon stands on the folded panel's edge (data-sf-resizer-unfold), its glyph the side the panel opens from (left_panel_open / right_panel_open). A fold is kept with the width ({v:1, width, folded:true}); a host keeps it as value 0, and resize says width 0. Without collapsible Enter still restores the default. (3) aria-valuenow is the share of the way from min to max, 0-100, aria-valuemin 0, aria-valuemax 100, aria-valuetext the words («27 %», «Свёрнуто»; lang value and folded), aria-controls the panel (an id is given to a panel without one); SF.Resizer.attach edges say the same (their caller may pass its own text). (4) Below the layout's split step -- the container's width under 40rem (--sf-h0), or a .sf-workspace region whose layout is narrow -- the handle is not there (data-sf-resizer-narrow, display none) and a fold is not drawn; the width and the fold the person chose wait for a wide screen. (5) Table column edges: SF.Resizer.attach leaves Enter and Escape on edges it does not own (options.handles) to their component, which takes focus back to the header; a double click calls the caller's reset, which for a column is the fit to content; the edge's Tab order is the caller's (one Tab stop for the table, C146(8)). The header menu (Изменить ширину · По содержимому · По умолчанию) and its words are sf-view-table's (SIMAI Pro). (6) .sf-workspace regions with data-sf-workspace-resize get their edge from core (workspace.js places an sf-resizer, collapsible on the list) -- the width in the region's variable (--sf-workspace-list, --sf-workspace-panel), kept as sf-resizer/<key>, written before the first paint by core.

number-type: min and max are CSS lengths with tokens (12rem, var(--sf-g3)), resolved in the target's context, so they stay strings; step is a number of pixels from 1; value is a number of pixels, nullable (no width kept).
own-verb-words: resize is a verb of the resizer alone (vocabulary §5 has none for a width); its word is lang events.resize.label. It reports, it does not ask: not cancelable.
version: 1.0.0 → 1.1.0: sf-resize is a dated alias of sf-resizer-resize, step and value are numbers; a minor while the alias holds (§4.10).

key-effects: role separator; ArrowLeft and ArrowRight step:-1 and step:+1 (step pixels, in the writing direction), PageUp and PageDown step:+page and step:-page (four steps), Home and End to:min and to:max, Enter and Space revert (back to the width the stylesheet gives, forgotten); keyboard.host says the same.

persistence (§7.5): the width is a person's view preference; with storage-key it is kept in this browser through SF.Preferences (persist local, key sf-resizer/<storage-key>) and the host may keep it for the person and hand it back as value; a leaf has no keys, so the manifest keeps it as these two settings.
base: the handle draws nothing, so it stays an HTMLElement: elementFromManifest over a host base that gives the scope (§7.7) and installs aliases.json (§16.20); the Smart renderer would add nothing.

target: the setting is its attribute (a selector of the ancestor to resize); the property target stays the method target() that answers that element, public since 1.0.0, so a page that calls it does not break; the property form waits for the next major.
template: none; the host is the separator and its line is a ::after of its sheet (scss/_smart__resizer.scss).
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json plus a remembered width, the inline-start edge and a disabled handle; probe.json drives the keys, the value and the alias.
skeleton: none; the handle has no data of its own: the target's width is the page's first paint, restored after layout.

side-effects: none outside its target: it writes the width (inline-size or the named custom property) on the panel it stands in, which is its job, and marks html[data-sf-resizer-active] while dragging.
css-variables: five public variables read by its own sheet (src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json).

version 1.1.2: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.

version 1.2.0 (resizer study control/research/2026-11-14-resizer.md, dispatcher ruling): (RS-1, C76/C58, D21) the strip a pointer finds is 24 (--sf-c2), 44 under a coarse pointer (--sf-d1), centred on the edge; the line it draws is unchanged; --sf-resizer-hit-size still overrides both. (RS-2) a target that clips its overflow (overflow other than visible: a scrolling panel, every .sf-workspace region) cut the strip in half and scrolled it away; the handle now stands outside the clip, positioned against an ancestor of the target (the target is no longer made relative) or, when the page positioned the target itself, against the viewport, at the target's edge as measured (data-sf-resizer-outside absolute|fixed, private --sf-resizer--x/--y/--h), followed on resize and scroll; a target that clips nothing is as before. (RS-5) ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move the edge the way they point in both writing directions: the engine applied the writing direction twice, so an RTL page ran its arrows against the edge (SF.Resizer.attach callers get the same fix: direction() is applied once). (RS-6) a disabled handle leaves the Tab order (its own tabindex is removed; a tabindex the page wrote becomes -1 and comes back on enable) and says aria-disabled. (RS-7) keyboard focus is the system ring around the strip, turned inwards, with the line in the focus colour; the hover line waits --sf-duration-normal before it shows (a pointer crossing the edge no longer flashes it), at once while dragging and on focus. (RS-8) the kept width (value, then SF.Preferences) is written while the element connects, not a frame later: the handle never shows a frame of the old width after it is defined; with the bundle on the page before the first paint the first frame has the kept width (a lazily loaded bundle still arrives after it). (RS-9) max also stops where the in-flow content beside the panel (a sibling on the same row) would be left narrower than min: the handle never takes the content's width; a stylesheet or page width over that room is narrowed while it lasts and given back when the room returns, never remembered. A page-written width is read as a length (16rem was read as 16 px when clamped).

version 1.3.1 (2026-11-14, owner decisions C173 point 7 and C181 (3), the layer roles): a patch. The splitter reads the sticky layer (var(--sf-resizer-z-index, var(--sf-layer--sticky, 50))); was --sf-z-index-7 (70). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

width.description: The width the person dragged to, in CSS pixels, clamped to min and max when it is applied.

folded.description: The panel was folded (collapsible); width is the width it comes back to.

attach.description: SF.Resizer.attach(root, {handles, session(handle) -> {measure, limits, apply, commit, reset, direction, step, start, end}, text}) gives any edge -- a table's column edges -- the same drag, keys, double click, cursor and separator value (share 0-100 with words); Enter and Escape on edges of options.handles are the caller's.

forbidden_client_responsibilities: saving the width on a server

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-resizer when a person should widen or narrow a panel, a menu column or a side area by its edge. Put it inside the panel; give min and max; write the width to the variable the panel's stylesheet reads.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not rely on pointer dragging alone; keep the keyboard path
Do not save the width on a server from the component; listen to sf-resize
ai_guidance.minimal_example: <nav style="inline-size: var(--menu-width, 16rem)"><sf-resizer min="13rem" max="24rem" property="--menu-width" storage-key="menu" label="Menu width"></sf-resizer></nav>

accessibility.focus: The handle (unless disabled, or below the layout's split step) is in the tab order with role separator, aria-orientation vertical, aria-controls its panel, aria-valuenow the share of the way from min to max (0-100) and aria-valuetext its words. Arrows move the edge the way they point by a step (Shift: four), Home and End set a limit, Enter folds and restores a collapsible panel (otherwise restores the default), a double click restores the stylesheet's width; Space does nothing.

sf-resize.summary: The width changed: while dragging (move), after a drag or a key (end), or back to the stylesheet's width (reset).
